heroHeadline: Iran-US Talks in Full Deadlock — Trump Rejects Counter-Proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE'; Oil Surges; Iran Warns Europe on Hormuz — Day 73
heroSubtitle: Day 73 (May 11): Iran-US negotiations entered full deadlock after Trump rejected Tehran's counter-proposal on May 10, posting 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' on Truth Social. Iran demanded US recognition of Hormuz sovereignty, war reparations, frozen asset release, and an end to all fighting on all fronts — demands Washington flatly refuses. Iran's FM spokesperson fired back that the US holds 'unreasonable demands.' Netanyahu separately warned the conflict 'is not over,' escalating fears of a renewed Israeli offensive phase. Iran issued new warnings to European nations against deploying warships to the Strait of Hormuz; the IRGC reiterated ships must use designated northern corridors near Larak Island, with other areas reportedly mined. Brent crude surged to ~$103.93/bbl and WTI topped $105 on deal collapse fears, reversing the prior week's optimism. US gas averaged $4.52/gal. Day 72 (May 10): Lebanon reported 51 killed including 2 medics in 24 hours of Israeli strikes on Lebanese Health Authority facilities in Bint Jbeil; broader Lebanon toll now at 2,846+. The ceasefire between Iran and the US — nominally in place since April 8 — is described as 'increasingly shaky.' ~1,550 ships with ~22,500 sailors from 87 countries remain stranded in the Persian Gulf on Day 73.
